title: UK's Sizzling Summer Set to Smash Heat Records!
summary: Have you ever felt so hot you thought you might melt? That's how kids across the United Kingdom are feeling right now. This summer is on track to be the hottest ever recorded there! The Met Office, which tracks weather, says that even if August has just normal temperatures, the summer of 2026 will beat the record set just last year. In summer 2025, the average temperature across the whole country was 16.1°C (about 61°F). This year has already been wild. A heatwave in May set a new record for that month. Then June brought another heatwave, and July had one that lasted two weeks in some places. The hottest day so far was June 26, when it reached 38°C (100.4°F) in a town called Lingwood in Norfolk. That's as hot as a very hot desert day! The UK has had 37 days in a row with a heatwave somewhere in the country. And for the first time ever, temperatures above 35°C (95°F) were recorded in three separate months: May, June, and July. August might make it four! All this heat has caused a drought—that's when there's not enough water. More than two-thirds of England and all of Wales are in a drought. About 45 million people live in drought areas, and over 27 million have rules about how much water they can use. There's been almost no rain for weeks. The forecast shows a tiny chance of rain this weekend, but it won't be much. For many places, it would be the first real rain in nearly two months!
why_it_matters: Heatwaves like this can affect your daily life, from not being able to play outside to worrying about having enough water, and it shows why we need to take care of our planet.

background_read: The United Kingdom is a group of countries in Europe where the weather is usually mild and rainy.
In recent years, many places around the world have been breaking heat records because of climate change.
The Met Office (the UK's national weather service) has been tracking temperatures for more than 170 years.
Article_Structure: WHO: The Met Office and people across the United Kingdom, especially in England and Wales
WHAT: The UK is having its hottest summer ever recorded, with extreme heatwaves and a widespread drought
WHERE: All across the United Kingdom, with the hottest spot in Lingwood, Norfolk
WHY: Unusually hot weather in May, June, and July, combined with almost no rain for weeks, has led to record-breaking temperatures and water shortages

perspectives.description: Some kids might enjoy sunny, hot days for outdoor fun, but the extreme heat can get so uncomfortable that it's hard to play or even sleep well.
Many families and farmers are concerned because the drought means there isn't enough water for drinking, growing food, and keeping animals healthy.
The Met Office tracks the heat to understand weather patterns and help people prepare for more hot summers in the future.
